correctness.rationale: The probability \(p_B(r)\) was independently derived by slicing B exact affine branches and directly confirmed using rational branch-intersection integration. Lebesgue invariance justifies each orbit-lag marginal. The exact iid reference is (N-1)(2r-r^2). For lag index \(k\le\lfloor\log_b(1/r)\rfloor\), the normalized excess equals one. For later lags, the difference from the explicit fractional-part F-kernel is uniformly \(O(r/b^{k-q})\); summing its geometric tail and the time-index weights gives \(O_{b,s}((\log N)^2/N)\). F has continuous integer joins and a uniformly convergent geometric series; its left derivative at positive integers gives \(\Phi_b'(0+)=-1\), proving the phase nonconstant. The actual standalone file verify_pair_correlation.py passed 156 rational cases and finite N checks. No finite test substitutes for these global arguments.

The exact endpoint-sensitive mean bias has a logarithmic law and a nonconstant lattice phase that do not follow from the circular metric or a mixing limit.
